method: Skeptic tree from git archive 4ec961e; run-copy with HOME/TMPDIR under the tree and PATH=/usr/bin:/bin (no opencode: the only opencode is /Users/nghinh/.opencode/bin/opencode, absent from /usr/bin:/bin). mutant_view.py confirmed every diff at line/function. child_evidence was called directly on the kill file's own fixtures (not_text, not_a_journal, broken_chain, torn_first_line, journal_is_a_directory, journal_locked) for baseline and for each of the 10 mutants (built via validation.v2.mutation.mutants(src,'child_evidence',_enum_members(src,'.'))[idx], desc asserted == the batch entry). The registered kill file tests/v2/test_v21_pw_lineage_unread.py was run one mutant at a time; the two non-registered account_of consumers tests/v2/test_v21_pw_lineage_spend.py and tests/v2/test_v21_x_lineage_gone.py were also run against the mutants that reach their branches.
measurement_result: Baseline registered kill file: 39 OK (euid 501, non-root, so @POSIX_USER tests ran). Each of the 10 mutants against the registered kill file: 39 OK == SURVIVED, reproducing the campaign; no REFUTED-by-measurement. pw_lineage_spend.py: 4 OK baseline and 4 OK on every one of the 10 mutants. x_lineage_gone.py: 29 OK baseline and 29 OK on mutants 35/36 (the only our-branch exercise it has, P.NOT_TEXT=b'\xff\xfe\x00 not text\n' -> L186, asserting only the wrapper 'cannot be read'). So no registered OR non-registered test kills any of the 10. Branch map measured: not_text->L186, not_a_journal/broken_chain->L197, torn_first_line->L200 (reconstruct succeeds, events==[]), journal_is_a_directory/journal_locked->L189. Every mutant left state==UNREAD and why non-empty.

entries.mutant: L200 string ' holds bytes and no complete event (a first line that was cut)' emptied
entries.grounds: Diff and branch verified. torn_first_line (self.put_journal(a_journal()[:60])) reaches L200 (measured: baseline state=UNREAD why='aisef-run.jsonl holds bytes and no complete event (a first line that was cut)'); mutant-34 why='aisef-run.jsonl' — the entire descriptive phrase is gone, the detail collapses to the bare JOURNAL.name, state unchanged. Unlike the L186/L189/L197 label mutants (35/37/41) there is no surviving interpolated diagnostic — the only interpolation on L200 is {JOURNAL.name}, so emptying the literal erases 100% of the cause. claim()'s refusal (lineage.py:311,317-323) then reads '...whose evidence exists and cannot be read (aisef-run.jsonl): it may have begun (UNREAD)...', which names no cause and misdescribes a journal that in fact opens, decodes as text and reconstructs (it was cut mid-write: the run began, continue from it — not restore permissions/encoding). No test asserts this branch's detail (confirmed by grep and by running the registered kill file + both account_of consumers: all survive). Asymmetric gap with the sibling L189 case, which HAS a 'PermissionError' content test (kill file line 235-236) and L200 has none.
entries.refutation: Input: the existing torn_first_line fixture self.put_journal(a_journal()[:60]). Reader: operator reading claim()'s LineageRefused ({unread}) at lineage.py:317-323, continue_from's report 'why' at bundle_cli.py:896, the CONTINUED-BY.{n}.json 'unread' record at lineage.py:331, and account_of's 'unaccounted' line at lineage.py:518,523. Sketch: add a content sibling of ChildThatCannotBeRead.test_the_refusal_says_what_could_not_be_read... building the torn-first-line child: state,why = lineage.child_evidence(child); self.assertEqual(state, lineage.UNREAD); self.assertIn(lineage.JOURNAL.name, why); self.assertRegex(why, r'holds bytes|complete event|first line'). VERIFIED to kill: baseline why matches the regex (PASS), mutant-34 why='aisef-run.jsonl' does not (FAIL). It pins the content a reader uses to tell a cut journal (continue from it) from an unreadable one (restore it) — the symmetric completion of the L189 coverage, not padding.

entries.grounds: L189 `e.strerror or e` -> `e.strerror and e`. Measured (journal_is_a_directory): baseline '...cannot be read (IsADirectoryError: Is a directory)'; mutant '...cannot be read (IsADirectoryError: [Errno 21] Is a directory: <path>)' — MORE informative (errno + path via str(e)), never less. journal_locked likewise renders '...(PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied: <path>)', so 'PermissionError' is still present and the content test passes. For OS-raised OSError on this branch strerror is always truthy, so `and` returns e and str(e) is a superset; the literal 'None' case needs a falsy strerror, which the OS does not produce here. Registered kill file 39/39 OK; pw_lineage_spend 4/4 OK. Matches the W2-lineage-2 index-55 ruling (an or->and OSError rendering, CONFIRMED AUDITED — verified in W2-lineage-2-v.json).
entries.refutation: n/a — AUDITED, no test owed. strerror is always populated by the OS here, so str(e) is a richer-but-equivalent rendering (errno+path+strerror); the readers show free prose and parse none of it.

entries.note: Author's AUDITED upheld; the richer str(e) rendering (errno+absolute path) is verbose but strictly more informative and unparsed — precedent-consistent with W2-lineage-2 index-55.

notes: All 10 entries CONFIRMED: every mutant is exactly as the draft says (line, function, measured why at snapshot 4ec961e), the four named detail-readers are real and accurately cited (minor line refresh: claim refusal 317-323 not 318-324; account_of 518/523/551), no reader of the detail was missed (continued_by reads only element [0]), and the measurement reproduces the campaign — 39/39 SURVIVED on the registered kill file for every mutant. I additionally ran the two NON-registered account_of consumers that reach these branches (pw_lineage_spend 4/4, x_lineage_gone 29/29 on the L186 mutants): neither kills any mutant, because their content assertions key only on the account_of wrapper ('cannot be read'/'unknown'/run.name) or the surviving 'PermissionError' token, never on the deleted label/delimiter/phrase. So no unregistered test refutes any audit. The one REFUTED (index 34) is upheld with a verified kill: it is the only mutant whose detail loses the entire cause and collapses to the bare journal name, which the readers' generic wrapper then misdescribes for a torn-but-readable journal; the owed-test sketch (torn_first_line fixture, assertRegex why r'holds bytes|complete event|first line') was run and does kill mutant-34 while passing baseline. The 9 AUDITED are upheld: 35/37/41 keep a unique interpolated diagnostic (e.reason / type(e).__name__ / str(e)); 36/38/39/42/43 drop only a paren or ': '; 40 renders str(e) (errno+path, strerror always truthy here) — precedent-consistent with W2-lineage-2 index-55 (CONFIRMED AUDITED).
